issues.quote: Before he left, did he say anything to you?
issues.fact: O3 says that as he went out he asked her to play for her, and she sat down at the piano at once.
issues.misreading: 'Before he left' can be read as earlier than the moment he went out, so the request might have come before the salon, or before the piquet ended, rather than at the moment of departure. That would loosen the start of her piano playing, which the sheet ties to his going out.

issues.quote: He said it was a sentimental object and not a useful one, which is what he always said about his brother's silver watch.
issues.fact: The sheet only says Félix's watch showed twenty minutes to nine. It does not say whose watch it is or where it came from.
issues.misreading: The sentence can be read as saying Félix's watch belongs to someone else (his brother), or is a different watch from the one he showed. That could make a solver doubt whose time reading the 8:40 was.

issues.quote: I do not look at clocks in this house. I have never needed to.
issues.fact: O2 says only that she did not look at the clock when he went out. The sheet does not say she never looked at a clock during the evening.
issues.misreading: The general claim that she never looks at clocks could be taken as a sign that her other time readings (the strike of ten, the strike of eleven) are unreliable or that she had no sense of the time at all. The sheet presents those as things she heard.

issues.quote: He is never without them between hands.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that the piquet went on until he went out to fetch his cigars. It gives no break between hands and no reason for the timing of his leaving.
issues.misreading: The phrase suggests he left at a natural break between hands, which could be read as a point in the game or a short gap, and that would give a whereabouts or timing hint the sheet does not support.
